<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video. Estimated time remaining: 10:00:00.</b><br>
  <sub><i>Working title. In development. The ETA is not a bug, it is the product.</i></sub>
</p>

One tiny island, one tall palm, one raft and one young woman in headphones. She mostly idles, nodding to the music, and every so often something happens: a message in a bottle washes straight back, a coconut lands on a hermit crab who walks off wearing it, a shark in headphones nods along, a ship sails past exactly while she is busy. A stationary-frame video for YouTube in the spirit of the ten-hour lo-fi streams, and an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, reimagined as a sunny coastal anime scene with a hand-painted look. 16:9, 1080p, always daytime.

There are more than 90 activities, most of them on four timers that go off every 2 to 5 minutes at the busy end and every 3 to 6 hours at the other. Each one starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code. Nothing is sampled.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

That is the whole install: a web page with a live preview of the island and an export to a YouTube-ready MP4. No setup wizard, no build step, no npm packages. Click INSTALL once; the waiting takes care of itself.

<details>
<summary><b>[ NFO ]</b> what you are installing, and how often anything happens</summary>

```text
 SETUP.NFO .............................................. CASTAWAY (WT)

 WHAT YOU ARE INSTALLING
   A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, ten hours long. One tiny
   island, one tall palm, one raft, one young woman in cream headphones.
   She idles. Every so often, something happens. Then she idles again.

 HOW OFTEN SOMETHING HAPPENS          IN A TYPICAL 10-HOUR RUN (MEDIAN)
   REGULAR ....... every 2 to 5 min ......................... about 155
   OCCASIONAL .... every 12 to 25 min ........................ about 30
   RARE .......... every 30 to 60 min ........................ about 13
   SUPER RARE .... every 3 to 6 hours .............. about 2, at most 3
   CHAINED ....... follow-ups, started by another activity
   IDLE .......... the rest. She is busy about a third of the time.

 THE SMALL PRINT
   Every activity starts on the next bar of the music: every 3 seconds.
   Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy
   with a coconut. Default run: 10:00:00, seed 1992. Same seed, same
   schedule, event for event.
```

The counts are the median of 200 simulated runs, as the header of [activities.toml](activities.toml) says. The file listed 94 activities on 2026-10-01 (81 on the four timers, 13 chained follow-ups), and it grows every few hours. `python tools/schedule.py` validates it and simulates a 10-hour run.

The renderer is a plain web page ([web/index.html](web/index.html)) served by [tools/serve.py](tools/serve.py). It previews live and exports frame-exact video in the browser (WebCodecs H.264, measured at 68 to 78 frames a second for 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two into an MP4. `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` renders a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display, from the older Python reference renderer. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults. Scene life has 26 entries: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

Status: in development. No video has been published yet, so for now the only way to watch is to run it. The working log is [MUSING.md](MUSING.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>[ MUSIC ]</b> every sound is synthesized from code</summary>

The MUSIC button opens the source, because a README cannot play anything. Every sound comes out of [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no stock loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. There are more than 150 sound files so far.

- **Theme.** A seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, a ii-V-I-vi progression over 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds: electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and the ticks and pops of an old record. One bar is also the scheduler's unit of time, which is why every gag starts on one.
- **Ocean.** The ambience is a seamless 60-second loop as well.
- **Levels.** The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and sound levels are adjustable in master and per routine.
- **Reviews.** None yet. Nobody has listened to it. It has been measured, which is not the same thing.

</details>
